title: LATAM STG 4 — FINAL v2
subtitle: Extended Interaction — Antonela confirms the delivered document has no legal validity: no signature, no stamp, unknown author, wrong template
location: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport, Santiago, Chile
classification: Attorney Work Product — Privileged and Confidential
violations_cited: CPCL Art. 197 — Falsificación en instrumento privado
CHIPENCOD Art. 211 — Calumnia (accessory by delivering false document)
LPDC Art. 23 bis (a)-(e) — Mandatory written notice of denied boarding reasons (non‑compliant)
LPDC Art. 3(b) — Right to truthful and timely information
CACH Art. 133 — Denied boarding compensation not offered
CACH Art. 131 — Duty to inform passengers of their rights

key_evidentiary_findings.finding: Antonela confirms the document has no signature: 'ninguno de nuestros documentos tiene firma.' A document without a signature is not a valid legal instrument.
Antonela refuses to stamp the document: 'nadie se lo va a hacer, señor. Va a perder su tiempo aquí.' This is an active refusal to authenticate a document containing false allegations.
The document’s author is unidentifiable. Antonela admits 'yo solamente la entregue' and attributes responsibility only to 'LATAM' as an entity, not an individual.
Antonela reveals the wrong template was used: 'esto no dice lo que a usted le pasó, es solamente para cancelamientos de vuelo.' The document is legally non‑compliant for denied boarding.
LATAM staff control the document’s content: 'solamente nosotros lo llenamos.' This connects directly to Diego’s instruction to 'ajustar' the letter in STG‑29.
Passenger confronts Antonela with his recording that another person asked her to 'escribir y modificar' the letter. Antonela minimizes her role to 'entregarse y,' attempting to disclaim authorship.
